A.tabline: Half the docks are idle and the main contact is leaving
A.headline: It looks fine on paper, but only about half the docks are really used, and the only person we talk to is leaving in January.
vs: All four forces are keen.
Only Westmere and Metro Central fly real missions. Tarn Valley has never flown one. Norwold only does training.
We're flying all the time.
True for Westmere (14 of 18 docks). Metro Central fell from 8 docks flying to 3 in October.
The alliance has the budget. Renewal will go through.
Nothing in writing. The person who says this, Rhys, leaves in January. Renewal needs a brand-new order by 28 Feb.
A 300-dock tender and a 30-dock stadium deal are coming.
Only Rhys has said so. No document, no date, no other name. Procurement said anything bigger must go through a formal process.
risks: Rhys Calder is our only contact and he leaves in January. Nobody else at the alliance knows us.
Around half the docks are not used. At renewal, someone will ask why they are paying for them.
Karen, our most active user, has been ignored: her battery email from August got no reply, and her urgent request for 5 Dec has no owner.
A document request from one of the forces (FB-10412) has been sitting with no owner since June.
actions: Today: take ownership of ticket FB-11206 and reply to Karen in writing – training dates and a named contact for the 5 Dec event.
This week: fix or answer Karen's battery problem on the two busy docks.
Before Rhys leaves: get a named contact at each of the 4 forces and at procurement.
Find out what FB-10412 is, and ask our Accounts team which force pays which part of the invoice.
Plan the renewal around what really works (Westmere, Metro Central), with a clear plan for the other two forces.
people: Rhys Calder – alliance drone programme lead
Our only contact so far. Positive but vague. Leaving in January, no successor named.
Insp. Karen Mbeki – Westmere drone unit
The real power user (62 logins in 90 days). A bit guarded because we have not answered her. Our best possible champion.
Procurement lead (name not recorded)
Said anything bigger must go through a formal process. Needs to be found and kept informed.
Metro Central, Tarn Valley, Norwold
No named contact at any of them.

B.tabline: Night patrols are stopping and finance is looking at the cost
B.headline: They say the docks pay for themselves, but only 4 of 14 docks ever patrolled every night, and now 3 of those 4 have stopped.
vs: 13 of 15 plants are flying.
Only 4 docks ever flew most nights. 9 fly about once a fortnight. One dock has never flown.
ROI is proven: about €1.2 million a year saved.
No breakdown has ever been shared. The only hard number is the insurer's 6% discount, about €180,000 a year.
The renewal is a formality.
Group Finance has asked for the cost per plant, and plants already dislike paying for a dock they did not choose.
Everything is going well.
In mid-November, 3 of the 4 busy docks stopped flying. The docks are online. Nobody told us and no ticket was raised.
risks: Night patrols are collapsing just when Finance is checking the cost of each plant.
The insurance discount (worth more than the whole contract) depends on the patrols that are stopping.
Stefan's deputy, who set up and runs everything, is leaving, and nothing is written down.
Stefan, who signs, has not logged in since May.
actions: Find out why the 3 busy docks stopped (AD-02, AD-05, AD-10). Check whether it is linked to the deputy leaving.
Write down the install list and patrol set-up with the deputy before he goes.
Meet Julian Tate (insurance) to protect the ~€180k discount, and build the renewal case on it.
Reply to Group Finance with the cost and value for each plant.
Ask Owen Fitch (IT) to fix the network at Plant 11 (ticket FB-10903).
people: Stefan Roy – group head of security
Signs the contract. Talks big numbers but shares no detail. Not logged in since May.
Stefan's deputy (name not on file)
Did the whole rollout and still runs the system. Leaving soon. Nothing written down.
Beatriz Alonso – plant manager, Plant 7
Finds it useful at night and would keep it. Her plant pays a cost it did not choose.
Julian Tate – insurance and risk manager
Got the 6% premium cut because of the patrols. Nobody in security has talked to him.
Owen Fitch – group IT lead
Can fix the poor network at Plant 11. Not yet involved.
Group Finance (shared mailbox)
Wants the renewal quote split by plant. Unanswered since 8 October.

K.tabline: Paid for, never flown, and the residents vote on the budget this week
K.headline: Kestrel Estates paid £14,000 for one dock in September. It has never flown, nobody there can fly it, and the residents' board votes on the security budget on 17 Nov.
vs: Everyone here is excited. We are just waiting to go live.
The dock has flown zero times in 7 weeks online. It was never commissioned, and Dana's one email got only an automatic reply.
The system will fly itself once switched on.
Nobody at the estate holds a drone pilot certificate, and training was left to the installer, who has stopped answering.
The dock is for mapping the whole estate.
What the estate really needs is night patrol of its two entrances.
Ready to use.
The insurer must be told about new aerial equipment before use. The dock has not been declared.
risks: The residents' board votes on the security budget on 17 Nov, and some residents already ask why they paid for a drone that never flew.
Nobody can fly the dock: no certified pilot, no commissioning flight, and the installer has gone.
Flying before the insurer is told could put the estate's property cover at risk.
Dana was promised a go-live plan by 16 Nov, and FlytBase has not replied to her email of 19 Oct.
actions: Call Dana Whitfield now: apologise for the silence and agree a go-live plan by 16 Nov.
Offer the pilot certification course for two estate staff (£4,000), so the estate can fly the dock legally.
Ask Lucy Pratt (insurance broker) to declare the dock to the insurer before any flight.
Book a FlytBase commissioning flight and set up night patrols for the north gate.
Give Graham Okafor a one-page update for the 17 Nov board vote.
people: Dana Whitfield – estate manager
Our only contact. Warm, but waiting since 19 Oct with no reply from a person.
Graham Okafor – chair, residents' board
Any spend beyond the original purchase needs the board's vote. Residents are already asking questions.
Lucy Pratt – insurance broker
Confirms the dock must be declared to the insurer before use. It has not been.
The installer (reseller)
Ordered and installed the dock, then stopped answering calls and email.

H.tabline: Busy quays, idle yard, and finance can't see the saving
H.headline: Brindle pays £96,000 a year for 6 docks. Only 2 fly every night, the yard dock is blocked by a privacy question we never answered, and the finance director who signs the renewal can't see the £400,000 saving.
numbers: 6 across three quays and a container yard
vs: The programme saves about £400,000 a year.
It is Marcus's own estimate of patrol hours. Finance has not seen the workings and no patrol contract has changed.
6 docks are a success.
Only D1 and D2 fly every night (183 of 211 flights in Aug–Oct). D3 and D4 fly about weekly; D5 and D6 flew 3 times in 3 months.
Ready to expand to two more harbours.
Marcus's wish only. No budget holder, no timetable, and the renewal itself is not safe yet.
Everything is running.
Elena's data-protection questions (FB-10231) have had no reply since 14 April, so the yard dock cannot go live.
risks: Priya Nair (finance) signs the renewal and will not renew on a saving she cannot see.
Tom Reyes, who knows the launch steps, patrol routes and alert rota, leaves in mid-December; nothing is written down.
IT moves the yard to a new segmented network around February, but has no record of what the docks need.
FlytBase never answered Elena's privacy request (7 months), which blocks the yard dock.
actions: Answer Elena Varga's four data-protection questions (FB-10231) and apologise for the delay.
Capture Tom's launch steps, routes and alert rota before he leaves (the £12,000 playbook offer).
Build a saving case with Priya Nair from real patrol data, not the headline figure.
Give Sam Okoye (IT) the docks' network needs before the yard network change.
Hold the expansion talk until the renewal case is agreed with finance.
people: Marcus Hale – head of port operations
Signed the order and champions it. Says 'it is my operation'; the only person we have spoken to.
Priya Nair – finance director
Signs the renewal. Guarded: has not seen the workings behind the saving.
Elena Varga – data protection lead
Waiting since 14 April for answers about footage. Her sign-off unlocks the yard.
Tom Reyes – rollout contractor
Set everything up. Contract ends next month; it is all in his head.
Sam Okoye – IT infrastructure manager
Not involved in the installs. Moving yard devices to a new network.
